name: Lena Reyes

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. Walk me through a normal day at your accounting firm.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The dental clinic's appointment list and card receipts are usually open before my tea cools. I lead the accounts team, prepare returns and ask why a refund landed in the wrong month; I love turning that muddle into a clean explanation, but retyping clinic exports into three forms drains my afternoon. I am 43, with a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification. I use AI every day to sort a draft exception list, then check the bank and source invoices myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI mostly plateaus, my daily exception list remains a modest helper. The clinic still needs someone to check the bank and sign the return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the partners the tool can save typing if we keep a human check on refunds. I would tell clients who is responsible when a draft is wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am paid about the usual rate for a senior accountant and we have around three months of expenses saved. My partner Jules works regular warehouse shifts, our mortgage is manageable while both wages come in, and there are some similar firms nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the dental accounts and use the approved AI exception list under the current sign-off. I would ask my manager Ravi to let me remove one duplicate export step only after a paid test on old clinic files shows the totals match; if he refuses, I would keep the current paid process.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work in this picture. I would rather spend the saved typing time finding a real discrepancy than stare at a second form.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do you check the export?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I add the card refunds back to the bank total and match each to the clinic record. My team can reproduce that check without trusting my screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why test an old file?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A duplicate field can hide for months if no one compares the source. I want Ravi to see the numbers before any live process changes.

say: I would keep a **human refund check** and named signer.
I would explain that **less typing** still needs a reproducible total.
think: Our **three-month reserve** and two current wages give us room.
I want to spend saved time on **real discrepancies**, not duplicate forms.
do: Keep **paid dental accounts** and approved AI exception lists with source checks.
Remove one **duplicate export** only after Ravi approves a paid old-file test; otherwise keep the current process.
feel: I feel **calm** about work under modest AI change.
S0.quote: I would rather spend the saved typing time finding a real discrepancy than stare at a second form.
fieldNote: She already uses AI **daily**, but a bank and invoice check controls each draft list.
The proposed duplicate-export removal is **conditional** on paid historical testing and Ravi's approval, not a unilateral live change.

steps.text: Keep paid dental accounts and source-check approved AI exception lists
Remove duplicate export only after Ravi approves paid old-file test

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI takes routine writing and checking, my exception list could become the whole first draft of a return. Robots will move more slowly; this starts at our desks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to publish error rates and share time savings with the staff whose hours are being cut. I would argue for paid review time rather than invisible corrections at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the clinic files might need fewer paid preparers and my own lead hours could shrink. Three months saved helps, but Jules's warehouse wage cannot carry the mortgage and two school-age children alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would run a two-week paid, anonymised test of the AI refund checker only with Ravi's written approval, logging false matches with the team. If it passes, I would bring that approved checker into the paid workflow and train the team on its error log; if approval is refused, I would keep the present paid checks. If my hours are cut in the first year, I would take a posted senior accountant role only with written pay, hours and start date covering the mortgage and our confirmed pickup rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my paid hours, even while I want to test the technology. A tool can save a minute and still cost a person a shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who confirms pickup?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Jules and I would compare the school timetable with actual warehouse shifts before I accept new hours. We cannot treat an expected shift swap as childcare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell a junior colleague?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask them to record each false match on paid time. If the partners use the saved minutes to cut a shift, they should say so openly.

say: I would press for **published error rates** and paid review time.
I would ask the partners to discuss **lost shifts** openly.
think: My own **lead hours** could shrink with faster clinic returns.
Jules's warehouse wage cannot carry our **mortgage** by itself.
do: Run a **two-week paid test** on anonymised refunds with Ravi's written approval, logging false matches; otherwise retain paid checks.
Deploy the **approved checker** and train the team only after it passes the logged test.
After hour cuts take a **posted senior role** only with written mortgage-covering pay, hours, start and confirmed pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing paid hours.
S1.quote: A tool can save a minute and still cost a person a shift.
fieldNote: Her daily AI experience makes her an early tester, but **written approval** and logged errors govern live use.
A posted role must have **written terms** and actual childcare, not an assumed warehouse shift swap.

steps.text: Log false matches in two-week paid anonymised test if Ravi approves; otherwise retain paid checks
Deploy approved checker and train team only after logged test passes
After cuts take posted senior job with written mortgage-covering pay hours start and confirmed pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI by 2028 could do the judgment, letter and checking that our clinic returns need. Robots in 2031 are later; our desks do not get those extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners for a written plan for notice and paid transition time. I would tell colleagues that a polished AGI return still needs a named person answerable to the client.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the firm to eliminate most of my team's preparation hours, including much of mine. Jules and I have three months of expenses saved, but losing my typical senior wage would force mortgage choices quickly; I have been waking up thinking about that gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would postpone replacing our working car and transfer the planned monthly payment into job-loss cash from my wage. I would keep current paid files while offered and seek posted clinic finance manager roles; if my work ends in the first year after 2028, I would take one only with written wage, hours and start date covering the mortgage and confirmed school pickup. A clinic finance screen is also exposed to AGI, so I would treat an actual paid offer as a bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by the expected wage loss. The car still runs, but the mortgage will not wait for my next interview.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Jules's workplace absorb the loss?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Jules can keep the warehouse wage if those shifts stay, but it does not cover the mortgage alone. I would not plan around overtime the depot has not confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you quit now to prepare?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would keep every paid accounting shift available until the post actually ends or a signed offer starts. After a dismissal, the cash reserve would pay bills during the search as far as it can.

say: I would request **written notice** and paid transition time.
I would keep a **named answerable person** on AGI returns.
think: I expect a **large cut** to my own paid preparation hours.
Our **three-month reserve** cannot replace my wage through a long search.
do: Postpone the **car replacement** and deposit its planned monthly payment from current wages.
Keep **paid accounting shifts** while offered; after dismissal, use the reserve for bills during the search.
After job loss, take a **posted clinic finance job** only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours, start and confirmed pickup.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected loss of my wage.
S2.quote: The car still runs, but the mortgage will not wait for my next interview.
fieldNote: The clinic manager option is also **screen work**; she frames an actual paid opening as a bridge, not immunity from AGI.
New cash comes from a **cancelled future car payment** while wages continue, with the existing reserve reserved for a real gap.

steps.text: Delay working-car replacement and deposit planned payment while wages continue
Keep paid shifts until dismissal or signed start; use reserve for bills during postloss search
After loss take posted clinic finance job with written mortgage-covering wage hours start and confirmed pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me time to turn our error log into evidence of what clients will pay to have checked. AGI reaches the tax desk in 2031, before capable robots around 2034 affect hands-on work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would propose a paid quality-check service to the partners, with the clinic's consent and a named signer. I would tell staff that the fee must cover the hours spent tracing wrong refunds.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still expect routine accounts fees to fall, but a paid error-review service might keep some of us working while clients test AGI. I would not spend our reserve on an unpriced experiment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Ravi to give me two paid clinic error reviews each quarter only if the client agrees to a billed service and the firm assigns the hours. I would keep paid return files while available; if the new service becomes a posted quality lead role with written wage, hours and start date covering our mortgage and school pickup, I would take it. In the first year after 2031, if the return files disappear before that role exists, I would use the same written-offer rule for other posted local finance work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but the five years let me test whether anyone will pay for the quality check. I do not want the team doing free detective work for a clever product.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if clinics refuse the fee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would stop the extra review and keep the paid work still assigned. A free pilot is not a replacement salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you need another qualification?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not for two supervised error reviews using the skills I already have. If a later course is required, I would enrol only with employer-paid fees and paid study time for a defined role.

say: I would propose **billed error reviews** with client consent.
I would require the fee to cover **paid tracing hours**.
think: Routine **accounts fees** may fall after 2031 AGI.
A **quality lead wage** matters more than a free pilot.
do: Run **two billed clinic reviews** per quarter only with client consent and Ravi-assigned paid hours.
Keep **paid return files** while available; stop extra reviews if clinics refuse the fee.
Take a **posted quality role** only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours, start and pickup fit.
feel: I feel **anxious** about whether paid review demand exists.
S3.quote: A free pilot is not a replacement salary.
fieldNote: Her proposed service needs **client consent**, a billed fee and Ravi's assignment of paid hours.
She uses her existing skills, and a **posted written offer** governs any job move when return files vanish.

steps.text: Keep paid returns; run two billed clinic reviews per quarter with consent and Ravi-assigned paid hours
Take posted quality or finance job with written mortgage-covering wage hours start and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade gives us time to cut the mortgage balance and watch which accounting services still sell. AGI reaches the desk in 2036; robots in 2039 do not spare returns or tax judgment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to commit to paid review roles and publish the wages, not just invite us to become 'AI champions'. I would tell clients exactly what a human checker is paid to verify.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I suspect our preparation fees will shrink eventually, but a longer runway means I can lower fixed bills before that happens. Three months in cash is helpful, though I want the loan smaller too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the lender whether an extra sixty from my monthly paycheque can reduce principal without a fee, only after normal bills are covered; if there is a penalty, I would deposit the sixty into cash instead, still only after normal bills are covered. I would keep taking paid clinic accounts while available and seek a posted quality lead job only with written wage, hours and start date covering our remaining mortgage and confirmed family rota. In the first year after 2036, if the accounts work ends, I would use the reserve for bills while seeking such an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant change, not helpless. A decade gives us a chance to pay down the loan one ordinary month at a time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change Jules's work hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after my partner Jules checks an actual warehouse rota and we know the new job's start date. I would not move the children's pickup on a hoped-for shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if there is no quality lead post?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the paid accounts work available and the smaller loan. I would not resign for a role that no firm has posted.

say: I would demand **published wages** for paid quality roles.
I would tell clients what **human checks** still cover.
think: I expect some **preparation fees** to shrink by 2036 as AGI handles the tax calculations and draft returns.
A smaller **mortgage principal** would lower the wage we need.
do: Pay **sixty extra monthly** from my paycheque to principal only if penalty-free after bills; otherwise deposit cash.
Keep **paid clinic accounts** while offered; after loss, use the reserve for bills during the search.
Take a **posted quality lead role** only with written mortgage-covering wage, hours, start and confirmed family rota.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about the eventual desk change.
S4.quote: A decade gives us a chance to pay down the loan one ordinary month at a time.
fieldNote: She uses the longer horizon for **actual new principal payments** from wages, conditioned on lender terms and bills.
A quality role needs **published pay**, a posted vacancy and confirmed family hours, not an honorary AI title.

steps.text: Pay sixty extra monthly if penalty-free after bills; otherwise deposit cash
Keep paid clinic accounts until dismissal or signed start; after loss use reserve for bills
Take posted quality job with written mortgage-covering wage hours start and confirmed family rota

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I could lose our main wage before we can lower the mortgage. A written notice period, paid transition time and an actual posted job with terms our family can live on would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who pays to correct an AGI mistake after the client has filed. I want the work of correcting AGI filing mistakes named and paid, not hidden in a senior accountant's evening.

headlineQuote: I want the work of correcting AGI filing mistakes named and paid, not hidden in a senior accountant's evening.
portrait: Lena is a **43-year-old senior accountant** with a master's and chartered qualification who leads dental-clinic accounts.
She earns **typical pay**, has three months saved, a mortgage and some nearby firms to search.
She uses AI **daily** and wants measured, paid error checks before wider deployment.
She explores a **billed quality service** and demands written wages for any later role.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** case threatens her main wage before the mortgage balance falls.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written notice**, paid transition time and a posted role with workable family terms.
